Opened the BBC first-chapter PDF, Penguin Random House excerpt, Penguin author Q&A, Guardian review, Independent review, Standard review, and author reading-group guide.
The reading-group guide confirmed multiple voices and perspectives but did not explicitly distinguish grammatical person, so it was not used as person evidence.
Search-result snippets, Wikipedia, informal blogs, and user reviews were treated as discovery material rather than cited evidence.
person_note: The novel alternates sustained first- and third-person sections rather than merely changing focal characters within one grammatical person. The quotes independently expose several participating first-person narrators and several sustained third-person passages. Authorized excerpts directly show a third-person Libby opening, first-person Jules and Josh sections, and a third-person Nickie section; multiple whole-book reviews explicitly confirm the mixed structure. Apostrophic references to “you” occur within participating first-person strands and do not constitute a sustained second-person strand. Dialogue, epigraphs, universal maxims, and clipped or isolated third-person subjects were not promoted to book-level evidence. No material uncertainty remains about the alternating first/third-person structure.
